title: Linkability of GPS telemetry to individual identity
description: Continuous GPS position data combined with timestamps in the data flow can be used to link sensor readings to specific individuals and their movement patterns, enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: GPS data is precise enough to identify specific locations and movement patterns

title: Identification through sensor telemetry patterns
description: Heart rate, step counts, and GPS data patterns can be used to identify the wearer's identity and behavioral patterns, even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Sensor data patterns are unique enough to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized access to stored sensor data
description: The wearable device (Process P1) stores sensitive personal health and location data that could be accessed by unauthorized parties if proper security controls are not implemented.
assumptions: The device has network connectivity or storage that could be compromised

title: Data usurpation for unintended purposes
description: The wearable device may use collected sensor data for purposes beyond the user's original intent, such as third-party data sharing, advertising, or insurance profiling.
assumptions: The device or its backend systems may have capabilities to repurpose data

title: Identification via GPS traces and timestamps
description: GPS traces combined with timestamps can identify specific locations and times of the user's activities, potentially revealing sensitive location patterns and routines.
assumptions: GPS data is precise enough to identify specific locations; timestamps allow correlation with other data sources.

title: Linkability of device ID across sessions
description: Device ID enables linking of data across multiple exercise sessions and potentially across different services, creating a persistent identifier that can be used to track the user over time.
assumptions: Device ID remains consistent across sessions; the app or third parties can correlate data using this identifier.

title: Excessive data disclosure to companion app
description: The companion app receives detailed GPS traces, device IDs, and timestamps that may exceed the minimality principle. These data elements could be used for purposes beyond the intended exercise tracking, such as location profiling or third-party sharing.
assumptions: The app may store or process this data beyond what is strictly necessary for exercise session tracking; data may be shared with third parties.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the app's data handling practices are not fully documented or audited.

title: Potential GDPR non-compliance via data minimality violation
description: Collecting and storing device IDs and detailed GPS traces may violate GDPR data minimality requirements if these data elements are not strictly necessary for the intended purpose of exercise session tracking.
assumptions: GDPR applies to the app's data processing; device ID and GPS traces are not essential for core functionality.
uncertainty_note: Assumes GDPR applicability and that the app's data retention policies are not optimized for minimality.

title: Unawareness of data sharing scope
description: User may not fully understand what personal data (calories, meals, weight) is being shared with the companion app and how it will be used
assumptions: User lacks complete information about data processing purposes
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.2 from context as it applies to user sharing personal data

title: Data in transit could be intercepted
description: Calorie, meal, and weight data transmitted from user device to companion app could be intercepted by third parties during transmission
assumptions: Data flow lacks end-to-end encryption or uses weak encryption
uncertainty_note: Standard assumption for data flows without explicit encryption specification

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: Companion app may share or expose user's health data (calories, meals, weight) to third parties without explicit consent
assumptions: App has data sharing capabilities or partnerships with third parties
uncertainty_note: Assuming app may have data sharing features based on typical companion app behavior

title: Linkability of health data to user identity
description: Stored health data could be linked with other data to create comprehensive user profile
assumptions: App stores data in a way that enables correlation with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Standard concern for any data processing system

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure to Data Store
description: The Companion Mobile App explicitly transfers GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store. This constitutes an explicit data disclosure of personal data (location is personal data under GDPR and similar frameworks). The disclosure is by design and necessary for the app's functionality, but raises questions about minimality - is storing full location history necessary, or could it be limited to specific contexts?

title: Location Tracking via GPS Data Transfer
description: The data flow transfers GPS location traces with timestamps, enabling continuous tracking of the user's movements. This creates a persistent record of the user's physical movements, which can be used to infer habits, routines, and sensitive locations (e.g., home, workplace, healthcare facilities).

title: Identification via Location Metadata
description: The combination of precise GPS coordinates and timestamps in the location history can be used to identify individuals, especially when cross-referenced with other data. Location data is inherently identifying and can reveal patterns of life that uniquely characterize an individual.

title: Health Log Data Disclosure During Analytics Processing
description: Personal health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) is transferred from the Health Log Store to the Health Analytics Service for health-condition analysis. This constitutes an explicit data disclosure by design, where personal data crosses a system boundary from storage to processing.

title: Health Data Identification Risk Across Sessions
description: Health logs aggregated across multiple sessions may contain sufficient information to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data. The analytics service processes longitudinal health data that could enable re-identification.

title: Location Data Exposure in Exercise Logs
description: Exercise logs may contain implicit or explicit location information (e.g., GPS coordinates, venue data). Transfer of this data to the analytics service could expose individuals' movement patterns and locations.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Location History Patterns
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) receives and processes location history data to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This processing may result in implicit disclosure of sensitive personal information about an individual's habits, routines, and movements that exceeds what is strictly necessary for the stated analytics purpose.
assumptions: The analytics service may derive patterns that reveal more than intended, or may share derived insights beyond the original scope.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a reasonable tree node for data disclosure at destination; context [5] supports Dd as transfer of personal data across boundary.

title: Identification via Location Metadata
description: Location history data in transit (DF7) may contain metadata or patterns that can be used to identify individuals, even if direct identifiers are not present. Movement patterns across sessions can be linked to specific individuals through their unique location sequences.
assumptions: Location data inherently contains identifying characteristics through movement patterns and temporal sequences.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a reasonable node for identification threats at the flow level; context [3] and [4] confirm I is applicable at fl position for DataStore->Process flows.

title: Profiling via inferred health insights
description: Inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags could be used to profile individuals or groups based on health patterns, potentially revealing sensitive health information about populations.
assumptions: The analytics service aggregates health data from multiple users and the insights could reveal patterns about groups of individuals.
uncertainty_note: Using L.2.2.2 from context as it relates to group profiling through data insights

title: Identification through health analytics sharing
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health insights that could be used to identify specific individuals when combined with other data sources, as health data is inherently personal and identifying.
assumptions: Health-condition risk indicators and trend flags are linked to identifiable individuals in the system.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard identifying threat node; context §4 confirms identifying threats relate to personal data

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data
description: The Companion Mobile App may lack proper cybersecurity risk management controls for handling sensitive health analytics data, creating compliance gaps with health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).
assumptions: Health data handling requires strict regulatory compliance; the app's security posture may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Nc.3 from context §2 applies to insufficient cybersecurity risk management with privacy implications

title: Data disclosure during analytics transmission
description: Health analytics data in transit between the Health Analytics Service and Companion Mobile App could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties, exposing sensitive health information.
assumptions: Data flows between processes are vulnerable to interception without proper encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard data disclosure node; context does not specify but this is a common flow-level threat

title: Linking of health condition indicators to user identity
description: The app shares inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals with the user, which could be linked to the user's identity through the dashboard display, potentially enabling third parties to associate health conditions with specific individuals.

title: Identification through health data in transit
description: Health condition indicators transmitted from the app to the user contain sensitive personal information that could be used to identify the user, especially if metadata or context reveals the user's identity.

title: User unawareness of data inference methods
description: The user may not be fully aware of how the eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals were inferred, what data was used for inference, or the implications of displaying these indicators.

title: Non-compliance with health data protection regulations
description: Displaying sensitive health condition indicators may violate regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection laws if proper consent, anonymization, or data minimization principles are not followed.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full health and location dataset is transferred to and stored at the cloud hosting provider, constituting an explicit disclosure of personal data across a system boundary. This violates the minimality principle as comprehensive datasets are shared rather than only necessary data.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a third party outside the organization's direct control and may process data in ways not fully auditable by the organization.

title: Data in Transit Disclosure Risk
description: Health and location data transmitted to the cloud provider is vulnerable to interception or unauthorized access during transit, potentially leading to unintended disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected against man-in-the-middle attacks.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard encryption protocols are in place but may have configuration weaknesses.

title: Metadata Linkability in Data Transfer
description: Metadata about the data transfer (e.g., timestamps, data volumes, access patterns) could be used to link individuals or infer sensitive information about who is accessing the cloud provider and when.
assumptions: Metadata is not properly anonymized or stripped before transmission.
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation of metadata handling in the transmission protocol.

title: Identification Risk at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud provider, having access to full health and location datasets, may be able to identify individuals or link data to specific persons, potentially exceeding the scope of intended processing.
assumptions: The cloud provider has sufficient data to perform re-identification or linking attacks.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the cloud provider's data handling practices and whether they maintain separate datasets.

title: Unauthorized Access at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud provider's systems may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, leading to potential data breaches of the hosted health and location data.
assumptions: The cloud provider's security controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the cloud provider's security certifications and incident history.
